$comment: THE ALLOW-LIST for the knowledge bake (plan §3.15). scripts/bake-knowledge.mjs reads
ONLY what is named here — there is no directory sweep, because a sweep picks up
whatever somebody drops into the corpus next month.
`never` is the refusal list from the plan's NEVER row. The bake matches every
resolved path against it and dies on a hit; it is a second lock on top of the
allow-list, for the case where somebody adds an entry above without reading this.
Tiers A and B are COPIED (scrubbed, then chunked). Tiers C, D and E are
`reauthor: true`: their content is NOT copied at any point. They exist here as a
record of what a hand-written replacement in knowledge/authored/ is supposed to
cover, and the bake REFUSES a reauthor section whose authored file is missing —
so the pack cannot quietly ship empty, and cannot quietly ship the original.
Licences: tier A is Apache-2.0 with a NOTICE (leanzero-forge-skills); tier B and
the authored replacements are ours.
F-956: `sourceName` and `purpose` are the two strings an ADMIN reads, and both are
authored HERE and nowhere else. `sourceName` is the human name of a source ('LeanZero
Forge Skills'), which is what the Knowledge tab prints; the source `id` is a slug that
means nothing to a reader, so it survives only in a title attribute. Because the name
now carries the attribution, the tier A licence dropped its redundant '(leanzero-forge-
skills, ...)' parenthetical and keeps only the NOTICE clause, which is the part that is
a licence condition rather than a label. `purpose` is written for the admin deciding
whether to switch a pack OFF: what it teaches, which surfaces read it, and what degrades
without it. No file paths and no code identifiers: a purpose that names a module is the
build talking to itself, and test-harness/scripts/bake-knowledge.test.mjs fails on one.
AUDIENCES are the only thing in this file that decides what a SURFACE can see, and
they are the easiest thing to under-declare, because nothing fails when a surface is
offered nothing — its field guide simply comes back short (F-539: `fix` was declared
on one entry and could reach 5 sections against a 12 KB budget, `validator` on two
and could reach 8 against 6 KB). The rule now, per source: `fix` goes on every source
whose sections are about FAILURE MODES AND CORRECTIONS, because the fix prompt is the
codegen prompt plus an error; `validator` goes on the sources a transition-time
question is asked of — Jira REST correctness, JSM audience and comment visibility,
automation semantics, and the platform facts about fields and JQL. A re-authored
source has NO per-file audience, so widening one means spelling its list out in full
(the bake's default is codegen/coder/agent/va/review). Widen by SOURCE; adding a
source is a separate, reviewed act. `test-harness/scripts/knowledge-select.test.mjs`
holds the floor: an audience with a budget of 6 KB or more must reach >= 20 sections.

forge-app-builder.title: Forge app builder
forge-app-builder.purpose: Teaches the models how a Forge app is actually shaped: modules and manifests, resolvers and their Custom UI, async queues, the platform's limits and cost, and the security rules an app has to pass before it ships. The Coder, code generation, validators and AI review read it. Switch it off and generated apps start guessing at structure the platform will reject.

forge-platform-facts.title: Forge platform facts
forge-platform-facts.purpose: The reconciled traps: what the Atlassian platform really does, as opposed to what its documentation implies, including rate limits, quotas and the failures that only appear under real load. The Coder, code generation, AI fix, listener and job agents, Virtual Administrators, validators and AI review all read it. Switch it off and the models stop anticipating the limits that break a rule at runtime.

cognirunner-sandbox-traps.title: CogniRunner sandbox traps
cognirunner-sandbox-traps.purpose: The mistakes this product has already paid for, re-keyed to the automation sandbox your rules run inside. Code generation and AI fix are sent its core on every turn, and the Coder and AI review read the rest. Switch it off and generated steps start repeating traps that were fixed long ago.

jira-rest-correctness.title: Jira REST correctness
jira-rest-correctness.purpose: How the Jira API behaves when it is asked to do real work: the recurring problem patterns, the error shapes, and the calls that look correct and are not. Code generation, AI fix, listener and job agents, Virtual Administrators and validators read it. Switch it off and the models write Jira calls that fail on the first real issue.

confluence-rest-correctness.title: Confluence REST correctness
confluence-rest-correctness.purpose: How Confluence is built and addressed: its modules, permissions and scopes, macros, page bodies in both formats, and the points-based rate limiting that throttles bulk work. The Coder, code generation, AI fix, listener and job agents, Virtual Administrators and AI review read it. Switch it off and anything writing to Confluence gets the page format and the throttling wrong.

jsm-correctness.title: Jira Service Management correctness
jsm-correctness.purpose: How Jira Service Management differs from an ordinary project: queues, request types, agent-only versus customer-visible comments, and who is allowed to see what. Listener and job agents, Virtual Administrators, code generation, AI fix and validators read it. Switch it off and the models risk posting an internal note where a customer can read it.

automation-semantics.title: Automation semantics
automation-semantics.purpose: What Jira Automation can and cannot be driven to do, including smart values, branch loops, and the limits that bite on large rules. The Coder, code generation, listener and job agents, Virtual Administrators, validators and AI review read it. Switch it off and advice about automation drifts into things Jira will not actually do.

administrator-practice.title: Administrator practice
administrator-practice.purpose: How a careful Jira administrator works: proving a negative before acting on it, judging the blast radius of a change, keeping a record of effects, and knowing when to speak rather than change something. Every Virtual Administrator turn is sent its core, and the Coder, code generation, listener and job agents and AI review read the rest. Switch it off and Virtual Administrators lose the judgement that holds them back from unrequested changes.

voice-rules.title: Voice rules
voice-rules.purpose: The house rules for how written output should read: the phrasings that are blocked outright, the ones that only earn a warning, and the hedges and stock openers that give AI text away. It feeds the wording checks applied to drafted comments and documents. Switch it off and drafted text stops being measured against the house voice.

scrub.$comment: The last four entries were PROVED necessary by the first real bake: the leak scanner found four provenance lines naming the internal apps and client engagements the docs were observed on (plan §3.15 predicted 12). They are deleted rather than rewritten because a provenance line carries no field-guide value at all.
SKILL.md line 16 names a client, a ticket id and a person. The named-line deletion is the reason this scrub block exists at all, and the leak scanner is the proof it worked.

The harness bed and its shared secret are ours, but they are operational detail that means nothing to a model generating a post-function — and HARNESS_SECRET is a secret-shaped word the scanner would rightly flag.

$comment: The laptop and workhorse fact memories. NOT COPIED — several carry a tenant host,
an app UUID, an account id or a client e-mail, and the value is in the FACT LINE,
which has to be re-stated as a neutral sentence anyway.
Two contradictions the plan requires reconciling BEFORE the authored file is
written: function-backed workflow conditions are a no-op while expression-backed
conditions ARE enforced over REST; and the Cloud Automation internal REST is
baked as 'no public create API; drive the UI', the earlier cloned-payload note
dropped.
workhorse _agent-commons/practice/*.md plus the client-free operating-model and
evidence-discipline notes. NOT COPIED: desk names and quoted corpus lines are
inseparable from the prose, so the replacement is written from scratch.
The generic BLOCK/WARN rule tables from the five linters. These become DATA for
src/shared/voice-lint.js (§3.11), never prose for a model, and no corpus line is
quoted.
workhorse atlassian-automation-builder smart-value and loop facts, plus the JSM
REST worked examples. Fact lines only, re-authored; project keys and app ids
never travel.
The 22 manifest/handler templates are 10-15 KB of CODE each. Chunking code into
2-4 KB prose sections produces fragments that are worse than useless to a model —
half a manifest is not a manifest. They feed src/shared/git-scaffolds.js from the
same source (plan §3.15), which emits them WHOLE. The bake reads this list only to
state, here and in MANIFEST.md, that it deliberately skipped them.
